blocks.text: A 45kg bale of graded vintage clothing typically costs anywhere from a few hundred to well over a thousand US dollars. There is no single fixed price — it depends on three things: the grade, the garment category, and the brand mix. Any supplier quoting one flat number for everything is a red flag.
What actually moves the price

Grade is the biggest lever. Grade A stock — clean, resell-ready pieces — costs a multiple of Grade C recycling stock, with Grade B sitting in between as the margin play for high-volume sellers. Category matters too: a bale of jackets holds far fewer pieces than a bale of t-shirts, so jackets price higher per kilo. And a bale heavy on Nike, Carhartt, Levi's or Patagonia will always outprice an unbranded mixed bale.
Do the per-piece math before you buy

Ask the supplier for the estimated piece count, then divide the bale price by that number. That is your cost per piece before freight. Compare it with what the piece actually sells for in your market — on Depop, Vinted, or your own rails. If the margin is not there on paper, it will not magically appear in the bale.
Buy the margin, not the bale.
What to ask before you pay

Always get four things in writing: the grade definition, recent photos of an actual bale (not stock photos), the size ratio, and whether the price is FOB or includes freight to your port. A serious supplier answers all four without hesitation.
For a current quote on Grade A or B bales, message us on WhatsApp — we reply with photos of real bales from our Karachi warehouse, not catalog pictures.

blocks.text: Most buyers import on FOB Karachi terms: the supplier loads your bales at the port of Karachi, and your freight forwarder handles the sea journey to your country. A 45kg bale ships easily as LCL (less-than-container) cargo, and first orders are normally paid by bank transfer (T/T) before dispatch.
Sea or air?

Sea freight is the standard for bales — far cheaper per kilo, and bales are not fragile. Air is only for samples or urgent restocks. Ask your forwarder for LCL rates from Karachi to your nearest port; for regular volume, a shared container slot brings the per-bale cost down further.
Realistic timelines

By sea, Karachi to UK ports typically takes around four to six weeks, and to the US East Coast around five to seven weeks. Add a week for customs clearance and inland delivery to your warehouse. The practical rule: order your next bale before the current one sells through.
Customs basics

Used clothing generally clears under HS code 6309, but duty rates and paperwork differ by country, so confirm the exact requirements with your freight forwarder or customs broker. A professional supplier provides a proper commercial invoice and packing list on every order — we do.
The cheapest bale is the one that clears customs without surprises.
How a first order works with us

You pick the category and grade, we send photos and a short video of your actual bale before it is pressed, you pay by T/T, and we book it FOB Karachi with your forwarder — or ours, if you prefer. Bales are ready to ship within seven days of payment.

blocks.text: A single-stitch t-shirt — one line of stitching on the sleeve and bottom hem — was the standard construction until the mid-1990s, so it is a quick visual signal that a tee is genuinely old. That is why collectors and resellers pay a premium for it.
How to check in ten seconds
Flip the sleeve inside out. One neat row of stitching means single-stitch; two parallel rows means double-stitch, the modern construction. Check the bottom hem the same way. No tools, no guesswork.
Why buyers pay more

Single-stitch usually means 1980s to mid-90s production — the era of the most sought-after prints, blanks and fits. It does not automatically make a tee valuable, but it puts it in the right age bracket, and that is where the money is.
Single-stitch tells you the age. The print tells you the price.
What else to check before paying the premium

Stitching is only one signal. Check the print condition — light cracking is fine, flaking is not. Check the collar: a stretched bacon neck kills value. And check the tag. A faded single-stitch blank with a dead print is still just a blank.
Our tee bales are sorted with stitching, print and collar condition checked piece by piece. Ask for the single-stitch ratio in your bale on WhatsApp.
